summary: Shows everyone knows, with a seasons twist: the casual found 8 and lost one life, the fan swept it in 10 guesses. Only Money Heist and Bridgerton Season 3 cost a life, both with a near-miss figure. It leans easy.
reasons: Casual: the plain names gave Squid Game, Wednesday, Stranger Things and Bridgerton at once, then Adolescence, Dahmer and "season 2" of Squid Game and Wednesday: 8/10 in 15 guesses. The one life went on Money Heist, which shows "106 million views" against 113.3 at #10, a fair near miss. The Witcher, The Crown, Ozark, The Queen's Gambit, Emily in Paris and Stranger Things 3 were free. Fan: 10/10 in 10 guesses, no lives lost.

The fairness problem is fixed, but now the lives barely matter: only two answers in the whole pool cost a life, so nobody runs out. The score comes down to knowing six shows and trying season numbers. A casual with 4 lives left would try "squid game 3" and "stranger things 5" next, so persistent players will land at 9 or 10. There is no real stretch answer, so curve is 3.

The data matches the page today (Squid Game 3, Stranger Things 5 and Wednesday 2 are in), every fact is good, "s2" and "season two" forms work, "season 3" alone says "be more specific", and subject words, films and non-Netflix shows are free. The Queen's Gambit, the real #11 at about 112.8M, says "isn't an answer" because Wikipedia has no figure for it. That is harmless but a missed lesson.
fixes: Ordinal season forms (src/game/match.ts, coordinator): "squid game second season" gets "did you mean Squid Game (Season 1)" (or "already found" once S1 is in), "stranger things final season" and "squid game final season" fall back to S4 and S1 the same way, and "wednesday 2nd season" and "second season of squid game" get "isn't an answer for this list" for #8 and #3. Read first..fifth and 1st..5th next to the part word as the season number. "final/last season" should get "be more specific" or be free, never the plain-name season. Guard: a real.test.ts case on a list with a part.

Other Monster seasons are corrected into #9: "monster menendez", "monster ed gein" and "monster the lyle and erik menendez story" get "did you mean Monster: The Jeffrey Dahmer Story", while "monster: the ed gein story" and "the menendez story" are free. A different season named by its subject should be free, like "stranger things 3".

Generic word: "story" and "the story" alone get "did you mean Monster: The Jeffrey Dahmer Story" ("toy story" and "true story" are correctly free). A lone common word should not offer an answer. Check the partial match on the alias "The Jeffrey Dahmer Story".
